hemoglobin.title: Hemoglobin
hemoglobin.meaning: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
hemoglobin.high: Can be linked to dehydration, smoking, living at altitude or other causes.
hemoglobin.low: Often linked to iron or vitamin deficiency, blood loss or chronic conditions.

rbc.title: Red Blood Cell (RBC) Count
rbc.meaning: Number of oxygen-carrying red cells in the blood.
rbc.high: Can be linked to dehydration, smoking, altitude or bone-marrow conditions.
rbc.low: Can be linked to anaemia, nutrient deficiency, blood loss or chronic illness.

wbc.title: White Blood Cell (WBC) Count
wbc.meaning: White cells are part of the immune system.
wbc.high: Often rises with infection, inflammation, stress or some medicines.
wbc.low: Can be linked to viral infections, some medicines or bone-marrow conditions.

platelets.title: Platelet Count
platelets.meaning: Cell fragments that help blood clot.
platelets.high: Can occur with inflammation, iron deficiency or after an infection.
platelets.low: Can be linked to infections, medicines or immune conditions; low counts can affect clotting.

hematocrit.title: Hematocrit (PCV)
hematocrit.meaning: Share of blood volume made up of red cells.
hematocrit.high: Often seen with dehydration or high red cell counts.
hematocrit.low: Often moves together with low hemoglobin.

mcv.title: MCV
mcv.meaning: Average size of red blood cells.
mcv.high: Large red cells can be linked to B12 or folate deficiency or alcohol use.
mcv.low: Small red cells are commonly linked to iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait.

neutrophils.title: Neutrophils
neutrophils.meaning: The most common white cell, first responder to bacterial infection.
neutrophils.high: Often rises with bacterial infection, inflammation or stress.
neutrophils.low: Can be linked to viral infections or some medicines.

lymphocytes.title: Lymphocytes
lymphocytes.meaning: White cells involved in immune memory and viral defence.
lymphocytes.low: Can be linked to stress, infections or some medicines.

esr.title: ESR
esr.meaning: A general, non-specific marker of inflammation.
esr.high: Can rise with infection, inflammation or autoimmune conditions.

glucose_fasting.title: Fasting Blood Glucose
glucose_fasting.meaning: Sugar level in blood after at least 8 hours without food.
glucose_fasting.high: Higher values mean blood sugar is above the usual range; only a doctor can interpret this against diabetes criteria.
glucose_fasting.low: Can occur after long fasting or with some medicines; a doctor can advise.

glucose_pp.title: Post-meal / Random Glucose
glucose_pp.meaning: Blood sugar after a meal or at a random time.
glucose_pp.high: Higher values can reflect a recent meal or reduced sugar control; a doctor can interpret.
glucose_pp.low: Can occur with long gaps between meals or some medicines.

hba1c.title: HbA1c
hba1c.meaning: Average blood sugar level over roughly the past 3 months.
hba1c.high: Higher values mean blood sugar has been running above target; your doctor interprets this against standard thresholds.
hba1c.low: Rarely a concern on its own.

cholesterol.title: Total Cholesterol
cholesterol.meaning: Overall amount of cholesterol in the blood.
cholesterol.high: Higher levels are associated with greater long-term heart and vessel risk.

ldl.title: LDL Cholesterol
ldl.high: Higher levels are associated with greater long-term heart and vessel risk.

hdl.title: HDL Cholesterol
hdl.low: Lower levels are associated with greater long-term heart risk.

triglycerides.title: Triglycerides
triglycerides.meaning: Fats in the blood, strongly influenced by recent meals, sugar and alcohol.
triglycerides.high: Often linked to diet, alcohol, weight or blood sugar control.

vldl.title: VLDL Cholesterol
vldl.meaning: Particles that carry triglycerides; usually calculated from triglycerides.
vldl.high: Usually moves together with high triglycerides.

creatinine.title: Creatinine
creatinine.meaning: Waste product filtered by the kidneys; used to estimate kidney function.
creatinine.high: Can reflect reduced kidney filtering, dehydration or high muscle mass.
creatinine.low: Often seen with low muscle mass; usually not a concern.

urea.title: Urea / BUN
urea.meaning: Waste product of protein breakdown, cleared by the kidneys.
urea.high: Can be linked to dehydration, high protein intake or reduced kidney function.
urea.low: Can be linked to low protein intake or liver conditions.

uric_acid.title: Uric Acid
uric_acid.meaning: By-product of purine breakdown, removed by the kidneys.
uric_acid.high: Can be linked to diet, alcohol, kidney function and gout.

alt.title: ALT (SGPT)
alt.meaning: Liver enzyme that rises when liver cells are stressed.
alt.high: Can be linked to fatty liver, alcohol, medicines or infections.

ast.title: AST (SGOT)
ast.meaning: Enzyme found in liver and muscle.
ast.high: Can be linked to liver stress, muscle strain, alcohol or medicines.

alp.title: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
alp.meaning: Enzyme found in liver and bone.
alp.high: Can reflect liver, bile duct or bone activity.

bilirubin.title: Total Bilirubin
bilirubin.meaning: Pigment from red cell breakdown, processed by the liver.
bilirubin.high: Can be linked to liver or bile-flow issues, or increased red cell breakdown.

albumin.title: Albumin
albumin.meaning: Main blood protein made by the liver.
albumin.low: Can be linked to liver, kidney or nutritional issues.

tsh.title: TSH
tsh.meaning: Pituitary hormone that regulates the thyroid gland.
tsh.high: Often indicates the thyroid is under-active; a doctor confirms with T3/T4.
tsh.low: Often indicates an over-active thyroid or a medication effect.

t3.title: T3
t3.high: Can be linked to an over-active thyroid.
t3.low: Can be linked to an under-active thyroid or illness.

t4.title: T4
t4.meaning: Main hormone produced by the thyroid.
t4.high: Can be linked to an over-active thyroid.
t4.low: Can be linked to an under-active thyroid.

vitamin_d.title: Vitamin D
vitamin_d.low: Common; linked to limited sun exposure or diet. A doctor may advise supplements.

b12.title: Vitamin B12
b12.meaning: Needed for nerves and red blood cell production.
b12.low: Can be linked to diet, absorption issues or some medicines.

iron.title: Serum Iron
iron.high: Can be from supplements or iron-handling conditions.
iron.low: Can be linked to diet, blood loss or poor absorption.

ferritin.title: Ferritin
ferritin.meaning: Marker of the body's iron stores.
ferritin.high: Can rise with inflammation, liver conditions or iron overload.

calcium.title: Calcium
calcium.meaning: Mineral for bones, nerves and muscles.
calcium.high: Can be linked to vitamin D excess or parathyroid activity.
calcium.low: Can be linked to low vitamin D, low albumin or kidney issues.

sodium.title: Sodium
sodium.low: Can be linked to excess fluid, some medicines or illness.

potassium.title: Potassium
potassium.meaning: Electrolyte vital for heart and muscle function.
potassium.high: Can be linked to kidney function or some medicines; worth prompt medical review.
potassium.low: Can be linked to vomiting, diarrhoea or some medicines.
